tools.name: count_text
tools.description: Use this when the user asks how long a text is, for example "how many words is this", "character count for this tweet", "will this fit in one SMS", "how long does this take to read". Pass the text exactly as written, at most 20,000 characters. Returns characters, characters without spaces, graphemes

tools.name: make_calendar_file
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a calendar file, for example "make a calendar file for this meeting", "create an .ics for my weekly class", "export these dates so I can import them". Pass 1 to 50 events, each with a title, a start (a date for an all-day event, or a date and time) and an end or duration

tools.name: make_csv_file
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a CSV file, for example "put this table in a CSV", "make a spreadsheet file from these rows", "export this list as CSV for Excel". Pass columns (header names) and rows (each row has one cell per column; cells are text, numbers, true or false, or null), up to 2,000 rows a

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_feedback_reply, index_tools · Private data: make_calendar_file, make_csv_file · Public sink: count_text, submit_feedback · Destructive: submit_feedback.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_feedback_reply, index_tools · Private data: make_calendar_file, make_csv_file · Public sink: count_text, submit_feedback · Destructive: submit_feedback

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
